subtitle: How Malik Ambar’s City Learned to Drink

panels.shot: sweeping bird's-eye over parched Deccan plain folding into a gridded canal network feeding Khadki
panels.action: Malik Ambar stands on a rocky rise overlooking the young city of Khadki, dry hills beyond, as stone channels snake toward its clustered houses and domes.

dialogue.text: In a thirsty Deccan, Malik Ambar backed engineers to bend distant springs toward Khadki—so his fragile capital could live by the Nahar-e-Ambari.

i18n.hi: प्यासे दक्खन में मलिक अंबर ने इंजीनियरों को दूर की धारें ख़ड़की की तरफ़ मोड़ने को सहारा — ताकि कोमल राजधानी नहर-ए-अंबरी से ज़िंदा रह सके।

panels.shot: slow push-in from shimmering heat haze to the dusty streets of Khadki under construction
panels.action: Malik Ambar, in simple court robes, walks through half-built streets of Khadki where laborers raise walls and dust swirls in the harsh sun.

dialogue.text: Around 1610, Malik Ambar shifted power to Khadki. Stone rose, streets formed—but the new capital gasped for water on the dry plateau.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1610 में मलिक अंबर ने सत्ता ख़ड़की में जमा दी। पत्थर उठा, गलियाँ बनीं — पर नई राजधानी सूखी पठार पर पानी को तरसती रही।

panels.shot: medium shot at a temporary well, workers hauling up scant muddy water as Ambar watches
panels.action: At a shallow well on Khadki’s edge, weary men haul a clay bucket of cloudy water while Malik Ambar studies the meagre yield, brows drawn.

dialogue.text: Local wells and tanks could not sustain markets, troops, and palaces. A city without a sure supply was a city that could not endure.

i18n.hi: मौज़ी कुंए और टांकियाँ बाज़ार, फ़ौज और महलों को नहीं संभाल सके। जो शहर पानी में पक्का न हो, वो शहर टिक नहीं सकता।

panels.shot: low-angle inside a modest audience hall, Ambar seated in thought, maps and scrolls on a low table
panels.action: In a shaded hall, Malik Ambar sits cross-legged before rough maps of the countryside, listening as an engineer gestures toward drawn hills and streams.

dialogue.text: So he turned to skill. Unnamed engineers, masons and surveyors brought knowledge of slopes, springs and masonry that the Ethiopian regent could patronize.

i18n.hi: तो उसने हुनर की तरफ़ रुख किया। अनाम इंजीनियर, राजमिस्त्री और नापतोल वाले ढलानों, सोतों और गारे का हुनर लाए, जिसे यह हब्शी वज़ीर सरपरस्ती दे सका।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ambar and engineers atop a ridge, sighting along cords and measuring rods toward distant ravines
panels.action: Malik Ambar stands with a small group of engineers on a rocky ridge, watching them stretch cords and sight lines toward a valley where trees mark water.

dialogue.text: They read the land. Gentle gradients from springs and streams west of the city could carry water, if cut, lined and lifted with care.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने ज़मीन को पढ़ा। शहर के पश्चिम सोतों और नालों से हल्की ढाल पर पानी चल सकता था — बस काटना, पक्का करना और उठाना था।

panels.shot: overhead view of laborers cutting a trench along a hillside, stone being laid in neat courses
panels.action: Lines of laborers chip a trench into the hillside while masons below them place dressed stone to form a narrow channel.

dialogue.text: Work began on the Nahar-e-Ambari. Intake works at sources outside Khadki fed a stone-lined canal, its path hugging the contour of the land.

i18n.hi: नहर-ए-अंबरी पर काम शुरू हुआ। ख़ड़की से बाहर के सोतों पर बांध बने, पत्थर जड़ी नहर चली, जिसकी राह ज़मीन की रेखा से लिपटी रही।

panels.shot: close-up of hands fitting stone slabs, water trickling between as plaster is smoothed
panels.action: A mason’s hands fit stone slabs snugly, another smooths lime-plaster along the inner face as a thin trickle tests the new channel.

dialogue.text: Gadkar later traced its hydraulic logic—gradient controlled, walls plastered, stretches covered, with sluices to manage flow and reduce loss.

i18n.hi: बाद में गडकरी ने उसकी जल-चाल की गर्दन पकड़ी — ढाल क़ाबू में, दीवारें पुती, कुछ हिस्से ढके, और बंध लगाकर बहाव थामा, नुक़सान घटाया।

panels.shot: wide shot of a large masonry cistern being built near the city, scaffolding and ramps around it
panels.action: A broad square cistern takes shape in stone blocks outside Khadki, scaffolds crowding its sides as workers haul baskets of rubble up ramps.

dialogue.text: Near the city, cisterns received the canal’s gift. Tanks stored, settled, and raised water, turning a narrow flow into reserves for seasons and siege.

i18n.hi: शहर के पास हौज़ों ने नहर का तोहफ़ा लिया। टांकियों ने पानी रखा, साफ़ किया, ऊपर उठाया — पतली धार को मौसम और घेराबंदी के ज़ख़ीरे में बदला।

panels.shot: interior view of an arched aqueduct section passing above a lane, with the city spreading below
panels.action: An arched aqueduct segment strides over a lane, its stone body carrying unseen water while Khadki’s clustered houses spread below.

dialogue.text: From cistern to city, channels branched. Some ran at ground, some crossed lanes overhead, distributing towards quarters, gardens, and the royal precinct.

i18n.hi: हौज़ से शहर तक नालियाँ फूटीं। कुछ ज़मीन पर दौड़ीं, कुछ गलियों के ऊपर से गईं, मुहल्लों, बाग़ों और शाही हिस्से तक पानी बाँटती हुईं।

panels.shot: courtyard scene with a newly built stone fountain fed by a spout, children reaching out to the stream
panels.action: In a sunlit courtyard, a simple stone fountain spills clear water from a spout while children and elders reach out, astonished, to touch the stream.

dialogue.text: Suddenly water appeared where dry earth had ruled. Public fountains and troughs turned the canal’s hidden path into everyday relief.

i18n.hi: अचानक वहाँ पानी दिखा जहाँ सूखी मिट्टी का राज था। आम फव्वारे और पानी की नांदों ने छुपी नहर को रोज़ का चैन बना दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ambar in a garden pavilion, water channels flanking planted beds
panels.action: Malik Ambar strolls along a garden walk in Khadki, narrow water channels flanking green beds and young trees in the Deccan sun.

dialogue.text: Sohoni places this within Deccan courtly urbanism. Gardens, baths and palaces were supplied, their refinement resting on unseen hydraulic craft.

i18n.hi: सोहोनी इसे दक्खनी दरबारी शहरी रंग-ढंग में रखते हैं। बाग़, हमाम और महलों को रसद मिली — उनका नाज़ unseen जल-हुनर पर टिका था।

panels.shot: documentary-style overhead map-like shot, showing canal line, cisterns, and branches sketched across the landscape
panels.action: A schematic view of the landscape shows hills and ravines, with a pale canal line running from distant sources into cisterns and branching across Khadki.

dialogue.text: Exact capacity and chief engineer remain unknown. Archaeological traces and later descriptions sketch only the system’s bones across the Aurangabad region.

i18n.hi: ठीक क्षमता और सर-इंजीनियर आज भी गुम हैं। बस खंडहर और बाद की लिखतें औरंगाबाद इलाक़े में इस जाल की सिर्फ़ हड्डियाँ दिखाती हैं।

panels.shot: tight shot on weathered stone outlet embedded in a wall, a thin stream still flowing centuries later
panels.action: A weathered stone outlet set into an old wall releases a thin, steady stream, worn grooves and moss hinting at long use.

dialogue.text: Yet the Nahar-e-Ambari’s remains endure. ASI notices and field surveys record cisterns, channels and outlets that once fed the early city.

i18n.hi: पर नहर-ए-अंबरी के निशान आज भी ज़िंदा हैं। एएसआई की तख्तियाँ और मैदानी सर्वे हौज़, नालियाँ और निकास दर्ज करते हैं जो कभी शुरुआती शहर को खिलाते थे।

panels.shot: low-angle inside a durbar, Ambar conferring with officers, a rolled canal plan on the floor
panels.action: In durbar, Malik Ambar sits among officers, a rolled plan of the canal by his knee, as revenue registers lie on another mat nearby.

dialogue.text: His patronage joined fiscal reform and urban building—but the canal was not his revenue system. It was separate work: masonry and gradient, not assessment.

i18n.hi: उसकी सरपरस्ती में माल सुधार और शहर-साज़ी जुड़ी — पर नहर उसकी आमदनी मशीन नहीं थी। ये अलग काम था: पत्थर और ढाल, न कि लगान।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ambar at dusk on the city wall, looking at lights and water-fed gardens below
panels.action: At dusk, Malik Ambar leans on Khadki’s wall, watching lamplight bloom across streets and dark bands of watered gardens outside.

dialogue.speaker: malik_ambar
dialogue.text: A city is held not only by swords, but by the water that feeds its breath.

i18n.hi: शहर सिर्फ़ तलवारों से नहीं, उस पानी से थमा रहता है जो उसकी साँस को खुराक देता है।

panels.shot: contrast shot: parched, cracked ground beyond the canal’s reach, and on the other side irrigated fields
panels.action: Beyond the canal’s line the ground lies cracked and pale; beside it irrigated fields show dark soil and rows of crops under the same sky.

dialogue.text: Design shaped fate. Where channels reached, markets and cultivation could thicken; where they did not, thirst and uncertainty continued.

i18n.hi: रूपरेखा ने तक़दीर मोड़ी। जहाँ नालियाँ पहुँचीं, बाज़ार और खेती गाढ़ी हुई; जहाँ नहीं पहुँचीं, वहाँ प्यास और बेयक़ीनी बनी रही।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of Aurangabad region evolving, older canal structures standing amid later buildings
panels.action: Across a broad view of the Aurangabad region, older canal structures and cisterns stand amid later buildings and roads, hinting at layers of urban growth.

dialogue.text: Khadki’s rise, Aurangabad’s later growth, and courtly life there were all made possible by such early waterworks framed within Deccan statecraft.

i18n.hi: ख़ड़की का उभार, बाद में औरंगाबाद का फैलाव, और वहाँ की दरबारी ज़िंदगी — सब ऐसे शुरुआती पानी के कामों से दक्खनी सियासत में गढ़े गए।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot of the canal stonework beside modern Aurangabad dwellings and traffic
panels.action: Old canal stonework runs beside modern Aurangabad dwellings and traffic, a quiet, worn remnant close to everyday life.

dialogue.text: Malik Ambar did not carve every channel, yet his backing let engineers bend distant water to his capital—a reminder that lasting power builds what people can drink.

i18n.hi: मलिक अंबर ने हर नाली खुद नहीं काटी, पर उसके सहारे से इंजीनियरों ने दूर का पानी उसकी राजधानी की ओर मोड़ दिया — याद दिलाते हुए कि टिकाऊ ताक़त वही है जो लोगों के पीने को कुछ बनाती है।

title_i18n.en: The River He Bent to Khadki
title_i18n.hi: नदी जिसे उसने ख़ड़की की ओर मोड़ा

subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे मलिक अंबर की नगरी ने पीना सीखा
